preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(n.is_integer() and 3 <= n <= 200000 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:t+1]])
preconditions.description: Each test case consists of a single integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 200000) representing the length of the array a.

postconditions.description: The first line of output is the number of test cases t.

postconditions.expression: all(len(lines) == 1 + m and all(len(op.split()) == 2 and op.split()[0] != op.split()[1] for op in lines[1:]) for lines in [stdout.strip().splitlines()[i*2+1:i*2+1+m+1] for i, m in enumerate([int(line) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:t+1]])])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output consists of m (number of operations) followed by m pairs of indices (x, y) where x ≠ y.

postconditions.expression: all(m <= n + 5 for n, m in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:t+1]], [int(line) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:t+1]]))
postconditions.description: The number of operations m for each test case does not exceed n + 5.

postconditions.expression: all(len([op for op in lines[1:] if op.split()[0] == str(i+1)]) == 1 for i in range(n) for lines in [stdout.strip().splitlines()[i*2+1:i*2+1+m+1] for i, m in enumerate([int(line) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:t+1]])])
postconditions.description: Each index from 1 to n is used as x in at least one operation (if needed).

postconditions.expression: all(any(op.split()[1] == str(i+1) for op in lines[1:]) for i in range(n) for lines in [stdout.strip().splitlines()[i*2+1:i*2+1+m+1] for i, m in enumerate([int(line) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:t+1]])])
postconditions.description: Each index from 1 to n is used as y in at least one operation (if needed).

postconditions.expression: all(len([a for a in [1] + [i+1 for i in range(n)] if a != 1]) == 1 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:t+1]])
postconditions.description: The final array for each test case must consist of exactly n-1 ones and 1 two.
